title: Missing since 1971 from Glens Falls, New York: Maryanne Wesolowski was only 13 when she disappeared
text:
2 hours ago Maryann Wesolowski. Photo by NCMEC website. Maryanne Wesolowski has been missing from Glens Falls, New York (Warren County), since August 18, 1971, according to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC). Her photo above (right) is an age-progressed likeness of how she might have looked at 62, though she would now be 68.
Some sites may spell her first name as "Mary Anne," but official websites like the FBI and the New York State Police spell it as "Maryanne." Some sources state Maryanne went missing on August 8, 1971, but official sources indicate it's August 18.
Today, 240 missing children in New York State are listed with the NCMEC, and the oldest case dates back to 1955. Notably, not all missing children are reported to the NCMEC, but they should be.
About Maryanne Maryanne was only 13 years old when she disappeared. She was classified as an endangered missing person. According to her brother, John J. Wesolowski's Find-a-Grave record , she has been listed as missing since 1971. His Ancestry.com record indicates there were 10 siblings in their family.
At the time, she was 4'6" to 4'-11" tall and weighed between 85 and 90 pounds. She has brown hair and blue eyes. She has a scar on her abdomen and chest. Maryanne was last seen wearing a white T-shirt, red and white shorts, and a black leather belt.
Maryanne was last seen on August 18, 1971, leaving her home at 44 Hudson Avenue in Glens Falls. She was walking to meet friends to go swimming at Haviland’s Cove Beach on the Hudson River, but she never showed up and hasn't been seen or heard from since. Go here to see her missing person poster on the FBI website.
Reportedly, Maryanne left a note for her mother, saying, "I'm leaving. I might miss you." She also wrote a note to her sister a few months earlier, which she never mailed. It was found after Maryanne went missing. In the note, she wrote about hating Glens Falls and that she couldn't wait for summer to start.
Maryanne's younger brother said there were problems at home. He was seven when she disappeared. He believed she left of her own accord and is still alive. Some sources state that her parents divorced in 1970, followed by the family moving to Glens Falls.
Another story that has circulated indicates that Maryanne was with a friend and one of her brothers earlier during the day at the beach. While there, she and her brother allegedly saw their mother's boyfriend with another woman.
When Maryanne and her brother arrived home, they allegedly told their mother what they saw, and Maryanne was sent back to the beach to tell her mother's boyfriend to come home. Supposedly, she was last seen near the intersection of Hudson Avenue and Spring Street in Glens Falls and was never seen again. There has been speculation that maybe the mother's boyfriend caused her harm.
Possible suspect One possible suspect in Maryanne's case is Kenneth Arnold Yarter Jr. In 1974, he was charged with the abduction and murder of 16-year-old Susan Camel Zanta in Argyle, New York. After crucial evidence was thrown out of court, the charges against Yarter were dismissed in 1977.
After 1977, Yarter was convicted of three rapes. One case was in New Jersey, and another was in Florida. In 1995, Yarter was charged again with Susan Zanta's murder. In 1996, Yarter confessed and pleaded guilty to second-degree murder. He was serving a life sentence in prison, and he died while incarcerated in June 2023 at age 72.
In 1971, Yarter lived in Glens Falls, and he worked at a restaurant that was near where Maryanne was last seen. He hasn't been connected to Maryanne's disappearance and no other suspects have been named in her case.
Since Maryanne went missing, her Social Security number hasn't been used anywhere in the U.S. She has a Find-a-Grave record indicating "Burial Details Unknown. Specifically: Missing, body has yet to be found."
Maryanne is listed in the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System (NamUs) under case #MP2876 . NamUs is an official website of the U.S. Department of Justice. She is also listed on The Doe Network under case #79DFNYcase #79DFNY . DNA is available for future identification.
If you have any information regarding Maryanne’s disappearance or whereabouts, call the Glens Falls Police Department at 1-518-761-3840 and reference agency case no. 5799-71.
You can also contact the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) through its website at https://www.missingkids.org or its 24/7 call center at 1-800-843-5678, and reference NCMEC #759895.
Maryann has been missing for 55 years. Every missing child's name deserves to be remembered, repeated, and shared until their case is solved. Every renewed search effort makes a difference, and every bit of attention given to a missing child's case helps keep it from growing increasingly cold.
Reporting to the NCMEC The NCMEC is not automatically notified of every missing child, which might explain why the number of missing children sometimes appears low, compared to other statistics. A separate report must be made to the NCMEC, even after law enforcement enters the missing child's information into the FBI's National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database.
When a child is entered into the NCIC database, the information isn't automatically sent to the NCMEC. To activate NCMEC's resources and support, law enforcement must submit a separate report to them . The NCMEC provides case management, poster distribution, law enforcement assistance, and analytical support.
The number of missing U.S. children fluctuates because many runaways eventually return home. However, some cases involve endangered missing people, endangered runaways, lost or injured missing people, family abductions, non-family abductions, and, unfortunately, foul play is sometimes involved.
Thank you for your time to read and share. Find Maryanne.
